options.title: Why does Denmark own Greenland?
options.first_line: Why does Denmark, a small country in northern Europe, own Greenland, the biggest island on Earth?
options.first_frame: The vintage map of the North Atlantic: tiny Denmark glowing red at the bottom right, a red flag already rising on vast white Greenland at the top, a dashed line drawing itself from one to the other.

options.title: How did tiny Denmark end up with Greenland?
options.first_line: Greenland is the biggest island on Earth, so how did tiny Denmark, way over in Europe, end up owning it?
options.first_frame: Greenland huge and white filling the top of the map, its name writing on, while Denmark's small shape lifts off Europe and slides across the ocean toward it.

options.title: Greenland belongs to Denmark. Why?
options.first_line: Greenland sits next to Canada, not Europe, yet it belongs to Denmark. Why?
options.first_frame: The map centred on Greenland with Canada's coast beside it; a pin on Copenhagen far off to the right and a long line stretching from the pin across the ocean to Greenland.

why: It sets up the puzzle you can picture in one second, Greenland sitting right beside Canada yet owned by a country far off across the ocean, so you stay to learn how that happened, and its first frame shows that gap even with the sound off.
